title: Undetermined Coefficients
short: Guess a particular solution shaped like the forcing term.
trouble: Students guess a term that already solves the homogeneous equation and do not multiply by t.

blocks.html: To solve $ay'' + by' + cy = g(t)$ we need one particular solution $y_p$; then $y = y_p + y_h$ by superposition. When $g$ is a polynomial, an exponential, a sine or cosine, or a product of these, a good guess finds $y_p$ with simple algebra.

Guess $y_p$ with the same shape as $g$, including every term that its derivatives produce, with unknown coefficients. If any term of the guess already solves the homogeneous equation, multiply the whole guess by $t$ (by $t^{2}$ for a double root). Substitute and match coefficients.

head: Forcing $g(t)$
Try $y_p$
blocks.cap: Then multiply by $t$ if a term solves the homogeneous equation.

blocks.html: These families are closed under differentiation, so $L[\text{guess}]$ lands back in the same family and coefficients can be matched. For example $L[Ae^{kt}] = A(ak^{2} + bk + c)e^{kt}$ $= AP(k)e^{kt}$. That fails only when $P(k) = 0$, that is, when $k$ is a root and the guess is invisible to $L$. Then $L[Ate^{kt}] = AP'(k)e^{kt}$, which works when $k$ is a simple root.

blocks.title: Exponential forcing
steps: Roots of $r^{2} - r - 2$: $2$ and $-1$; 3 is not a root, so try $Ae^{3t}$.

blocks.title: Cosine forcing
steps: Try $y_p = A\cos t + B\sin t$: $y_p' = -A\sin t + B\cos t$, $y_p'' = -A\cos t - B\sin t$.

blocks.title: When the guess is already a solution
steps: $r = 2$ is a root, so $Ae^{2t}$ would give $L[Ae^{2t}] = 0$. Try $y_p = Ate^{2t}$.

blocks.html: Guessing a term that already solves the homogeneous equation: for $y'' - y' - 2y = 6e^{2t}$, the guess $Ae^{2t}$ leads to $0 = 6e^{2t}$, which is impossible. Always find the homogeneous roots first and compare. Another slip: using only $A\cos\omega t$ when $g$ is a cosine; the derivative produces a sine, so the guess needs $B\sin\omega t$ too.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: The solution of $y'' + 2y' + 5y = 10\cos t$ that starts at rest (solid) and the particular solution $2\cos t + \sin t$ (dashed). The homogeneous part dies out, so after a few seconds only $y_p$ is left: the steady response.
